title: int8-attention-fusion-with-smoothed-scale-scheduler-and-kv-align
author: Aisha K. Patel
description:
Motivation: On long sequence workloads INT8 inference showed sporadic tail-latency spikes and suboptimal throughput due to misaligned per-head requant offsets, attention KV prefetch thrash, and coarse batching schedules. This PR implements a smoothed per-head scale scheduler that blends requant parameters across adjacent tokens, an attention prefetch kernel tuned for INT8 microkernels, and a lightweight KV cache alignment patch that reduces redundant page faults when continuous batching is active.

Summary of changes: implemented a SmoothedScaleScheduler that computes an exponentially-weighted moving average over head scales and applies a runtime-corrected requant offset during attention matmul; added an INT8-prefetch attention CUDA microkernel with aligned loads and prefetch hints; patched KV cache allocator to maintain 64B-aligned slices for INT8/FP8 packed tensors and added a no-copy fastpath for KV reads when alignment holds; integrated scheduler hooks with continuous_batcher so short-lived bursts are coalesced without increasing headroom. Exposed a new runtime flag --quant-smoothing-window and an experimental --prefer-fp8 path toggle for model teams to A/B.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for SmoothedScaleScheduler math; [x] microkernel integration tests; [x] end-to-end perf bench; [x] docs note in optimize/quantization.md; [x] rollout plan (gradual).

Testing & Benchmarks: See benchmark_summary field for top-line numbers. Microbenchmarks included token-level verification that requant maintains numerical parity with baseline within 1.5% KL for sampling workloads. Stress tests (10k concurrent short requests) show 12-18% throughput improvement and 20-30% reduction in p99 latency regressions tied to KV page faults.

Backward compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior (smoothing window = 0). The FP8 toggle is opt-in and gated behind feature flags; no model code changes required unless teams opt-in for FP8 packing.

Rollout plan: merge to main but feature-gated. Canary to Dedicated region us-west-2 with 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor p95/p99, token error-rate and quality regressions through existing evals. If stable, increase to 25% then 100% over one week.

Notes: This is focused on inference serving; build changes add a small runtime dependency on the microkernel test harness but do not change public API surfaces.

review_thread:
Daniel: Can you explain the smoothing hyperparameters and why EWMA instead of simple windowed median?
Aisha: EWMA gives a low-overhead single-pass update and better reacts to sustained shifts; default alpha maps to approx a 16-token half-life which we tuned on conversation workloads.
Linnea: The KV alignment change looks risky for older private installs due to allocator differences. Can we gate behavioral change?
Aisha: Gate is implemented; allocator keeps legacy slowpath when alignment cannot be guaranteed. Added explicit migration log lines.
Ravi: I saw a small numeric delta on sampling outputs for one of our tests. Is it acceptable?
Aisha: Diffs are <1.5% KL; added a guard to switch off smoothing when the model exposes non-deterministic requant behavior.
Linnea: CI green except perf flake; re-run perf pipeline after fixes.
Aisha: Perf pipeline re-run completed and green. Reviewed by Daniel and Linnea; approved with squash merge.
release_notes: Improves INT8 attention performance by adding a smoothed per-head requant scheduler, an INT8 attention prefetch microkernel, and KV cache alignment optimizations. Opt-in FP8 path and smoothing window available via runtime flags. Improves throughput and tail-latency for long-sequence workloads; feature-gated and canaryed before full rollout.
notes_for_ops: Deployment: enable feature via runtime flag --quant-smoothing-window=N (default 0). For dedicated/private, ensure allocator migration log is observed and rollback flag --quant-smoothing-window=0 is available. Monitor metrics: runtime.attn.requant_applied, runtime.kv.alignment_hits, p95_latency, token_error_rate. Canary plan: us-west-2 5% -> 25% -> 100%.
benchmark_summary: Microbenchmarks (NVIDIA T4-like instance, batch sizes representative of PLG traffic): INT8 end-to-end P95 latency: baseline 42ms -> 31ms (26% reduction). Throughput: baseline 820 tokens/s -> 967 tokens/s (+18%). p99 latency improved 34% in bursty short-request tests. Memory overhead: +6% for small EWMA state per head. Sampling quality delta: KL<1.5% vs baseline. FP8 opt-in path showed an additional ~6% throughput gain in internal tests (experimental).
